title: Multi-statement atomicity is expressed through batch; no partial result is ever surfaced
asA: developer whose domain operations require two or more statements to land as one unit or none
iWant: the facade to issue such operations through `db.batch([...])` and to surface no partial-batch result on any failure path
soThat: a consumer never has to reason about 'some statements landed, some did not' and mid-batch failures roll back cleanly

acceptanceCriteria.description: Every facade verb whose implementation requires multi-statement atomicity issues its statements through a single `db.batch([...])` invocation; the facade does not synthesise atomicity by issuing sequential `db.prepare(...).run()` calls under an application-side try-catch.
acceptanceCriteria.when: every verb whose responsibility involves writing to two or more rows across two or more statements is inspected
acceptanceCriteria.then: each such verb issues its statements as one `db.batch([...])` call whose array contains every statement the atomicity claim covers, and no such verb chains sequential independent facade calls to fake atomicity

acceptanceCriteria.description: A facade verb whose batch fails mid-sequence (a UNIQUE constraint violation on the second statement of a two-statement batch) surfaces the failure to the caller without persisting the first statement.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a facade verb that batches an insert into table A followed by a constraint-violating insert into table B, and a local D1 database primed to violate the constraint
acceptanceCriteria.when: the verb is invoked and the batch fails
acceptanceCriteria.then: the caller receives an error, and a follow-up read against table A shows no row corresponding to the first statement of the failed batch (D1 rolled the batch back)

acceptanceCriteria.description: The facade does not export a public method whose contract implies atomicity across two separate facade calls; consumers do not chain facade calls under a transaction assumption because no facade surface offers one.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the facade module's public surface and any documentation the facade emits
acceptanceCriteria.when: the surface is inspected for begin/commit primitives, transaction-block wrappers, or documentation promising cross-call atomicity
acceptanceCriteria.then: no such surface exists on the facade, and every atomicity claim in facade documentation is scoped to a single verb whose implementation uses `db.batch([...])`
